entries.title: Monthly Entitlements to the Data Lake

steps.title: One batch, three delivery designs
steps.description: Larkspur Library is a fictional subscription service. Each month it records which guides and books its customers can access, then delivers an auditable history to a data lake. A writes every subscription–item pair, B stores subscription grants alongside a snapshot of the monthly catalog, and C delivers immutable Parquet files. The volumes and prices in this study are scenario assumptions and estimates. Zoom in to read the full comparison board, or use the steps to explore each design.

Estimated Monthly Cost · Google Cloud List-Price Model (USD and BRL)

Total = database + data + processing. A/B use a dedicated 2 vCPU / 8 GB database (~US$ 134, double with HA). C uses a small instance (~US$ 15).
Data: ~200 B per Postgres row, ~20 B per Parquet row, ~30 items per subscription. A/B use Datastream CDC at US$ 2 per GiB in the model.
Processing: ~US$ 5 per 100 million at 500 records/s on 1 vCPU. Excludes data lake and engineering time.
The model uses approximate São Paulo Cloud SQL pricing and R$ 5.55 per US dollar (reference closing rate R$ 5.56).
Up to 100 million records, the database instance dominates the estimate.
Study scale: 158 million active subscriptions. A and C write about 4.7 billion records at roughly 30 items per subscription.
A needs a larger instance. B writes 158 million rows. C at the same subscription grain is about US$ 25.
Cost Breakdown at 100 Million Records per Month (USD and BRL)

• Job state: prevent overlapping runs and time out orphaned running records
• Persist the cursor in the batch transaction
• Separate writer, purge and CDC privileges. Limit CDC to published tables
• A/B: set max_slot_wal_keep_size and alert on replication lag
• C: derive the object key from the batch, then create only if absent
• Entitlements Postgres: read-only access, keyset paging and small batches without a replica
• Registry: coordinate a replica or materialized view with the DBA. Avoid primary reads
• Registry view exposes ID, plan, status and dates. Exclude document IDs, email and phone
• Registry lacks a date index. Page by subscriptions.id and parallelize by ID range
• Registry holds current state. Snapshot at month-end. Order history lives in orders
• Incremental runs replay a recent window. Set a fixed cutoff timezone
• Send failed subscriptions to an error table and continue the batch
• Send a month-closed signal and per-run count to the lake
• LGPD: define lake retention and a data-subject deletion flow
• Rundeck: restrict triggers with ACLs, prevent concurrent runs, use Key Storage and omit PII

• Can access be revoked? The answer governs corrections.
• Is the subscription ID sufficient? Product and engineering to confirm.
• Does the registry already feed the lake? The join could happen there.
• Can history share Entitlements Postgres? Who provisions it?
• Where should it run (Cloud Run Jobs, Kubernetes or a Rundeck node)?
• How does CDC handle DROP PARTITION and DELETE?
• Who owns the registry read replica or view, and what is the lead time?
• Can orders reconstruct effective dates for a closed month?

• B: use subscription-grain grants at the 158M-subscription study scale
• A: roughly 4.7 billion rows per month makes per-item materialization impractical
• C: consider files at subscription grain, matching B
• A registry replica or view introduces a DBA dependency for delivery
• At study scale, per-item expansion dominates modeled cost

Proposal for review · Option A is the baseline after an engineering discussion · Redis was ruled out for this workflow's transactional needs · Scale assumption: 158 million active subscriptions
Subscription is the key · Monthly processing with daily backfill · No replica for Entitlements Postgres. Read it in small batches. Read the registry through a replica or materialized view because direct database access and an API are outside the source team's scope.

steps.title: A · Materialized Entitlements (Baseline)
steps.description: Insert-only Postgres + CDC · One row per subscription × item × reporting month. Baseline proposal, easy to explain. Query customer entitlements directly in Postgres. Roughly 4.7 billion rows per month at study scale. No snapshot. Depends on source state at run time. Upgrades and refunds have no correction path.

steps.title: B · Grants + Catalog Snapshot
steps.description: Postgres + CDC · One row per subscription · The data lake joins both tables. One row per subscription. Saved catalog snapshot makes results reproducible. Keeps Postgres and CDC. Assumes access follows plan, tier and period. The data team owns the join.

steps.title: C · Immutable Files in Object Storage
steps.description: Postgres tracks job state · Retention-locked Parquet files · No CDC. Retention lock makes files immutable. No replication slot or database purge. Retries target the same file key. Customer lookup waits for data lake ingestion. Harder to test and requires file ingestion.
